chunks.text: Now when we read SPY, we get all the potential dates and all the prices that go with that. And in this case, we're loading adjusted close data. Note that there's many more dates here than there are here. And this is our target data frame that we loaded with the particular dates

chunks.text: that we're interested in. One other thing to mention that I didn't mention before is these two days are weekend days. chunks.title: How We're Going to do it
chunks.text: So if you compare this with this, look, in our SPY history, we don't have the 23rd and the 24th because SPY did not trade that day. Because if SPY traded, it meant the market was open.

chunks.title: How We're Going to do it
chunks.text: And if the market was open, SPY traded. So SPY, the S&P 500 ETF, is our reference for many, many things.
